title: Why Stopping Antibiotics Early Is Dangerous
description:
Why do doctors insist on completing a full course of antibiotics instead of stopping the moment you feel better? Some alternative medicine advocates claim it’s just to sell more pills — but the truth lies in evolution.

This video explains how antibiotics work against bacterial infections, why some bacteria are more resistant than others, and what happens when you stop your treatment early. You kill off the weaker bacteria first, leaving the strongest, toughest strains to survive and multiply. This creates what biologists call a bottleneck effect — a reduction in population size that leaves behind only the most resistant survivors.

We explore how this evolutionary pressure drives the development of more dangerous, resistant bacteria. Just like natural disasters create genetic bottlenecks in wildlife, incomplete antibiotic use fuels antibiotic resistance, one of the biggest medical challenges of our time.

If you’ve searched for “why finish antibiotics course,” “antibiotic resistance explained,” “bottleneck effect evolution,” “genetic drift examples,” “directional selection in bacteria,” or “evidence for evolution”, this video shows how everyday medicine demonstrates evolution in action.
